chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala and Hammam from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

When the sun sets, perform the Ihram (Ifadah) with the people, and upon you be calmness and dignity, and perform Ihram 'from where the people perform Ihram', and seek forgiveness of 'Allah, indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful'. When you reach the red sand dune - on the right of the road - say: 'O Allah, have mercy on my standing, increase in my deeds, preserve for me my religion, and accept my rituals, and spare me from the 'burden' (wadhif) which many people do, for it has reached us that Hajj is not the burdening of horses nor the wasting of camels, but fear Allah and walk a beautiful walk, and do not tread on the weak, nor tread on a Muslim, and be moderate in walking, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to restrain his she-camel until its head would reach the front of the saddle, and he would say: 'O people, upon you is composure, so the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is to be followed.'

Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'O Allah, free me from the Fire,' repeating it until the people performed Ihram. I said: 'Will you not perform Ihram, for the people have performed Ihram?' He said: 'I fear the crowding, and I fear that I will share in the hardship of a person.'

key_terms.إِفَاضَة: The ritual departure or Ihram from Arafat

ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette and behavior for pilgrims when performing Ihram from Arafat?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides detailed practical guidance for the Ifadah from Arafat, emphasizing *sakinah* (tranquility) and *waqar* (dignity) while urging pilgrims to avoid the rush (*zihmam*) to prevent the hardship (*anat*) of the crowd. It connects the physical act of departure with spiritual introspection, citing the Prophet’s (PBUH) moderation in travel as a model for avoiding the burdening of weaker pilgrims. The narration underscores the Shia emphasis on balancing ritual performance with social consideration and spiritual mindfulness during the Hajj rites.
